title: Tobacco fortunes and the streets they built
episode: 65. The Tobacco Lords & the Slave Trade: Merchant City, Glasgow
spotify: Neil Oliver Podcast The Tobacco Lords & the Slave Trade Merchant City Glasgow
apple: Neil Oliver Podcast The Tobacco Lords & the Slave Trade Merchant City Glasgow
description: Historian and broadcaster Neil Oliver on Glasgow’s 18th-century tobacco lords, whose wealth came from plantations worked by enslaved people, and on the Merchant City, the quarter of streets and mansions they built east of George Square.

title: Saint, cathedral, trading port, workshop of the Empire
description: A one-episode history of Glasgow, which grew up around the medieval cathedral of St Mungo, the city’s patron saint, and became a transatlantic trading port and then one of the world’s great shipbuilding and engineering cities.

title: Sixty-six fans die on a stairway after a New Year derby
spotify: Only Our Rivers Run Free The Ibrox Disaster January 1971
apple: Only Our Rivers Run Free The Ibrox Disaster January 1971
description: On 2 January 1971, as fans left the Old Firm derby between Glasgow’s two big clubs, Rangers and Celtic, a crush on Stairway 13 at Ibrox Stadium killed 66 people. The disaster led to Britain’s first stadium safety law in 1975.

title: Gangs, vans and a fatal fire in the housing schemes
episode: 6 - The Glasgow Ice Cream Truck Wars
spotify: The Dollop The Glasgow Ice Cream Truck Wars
apple: The Dollop The Glasgow Ice Cream Truck Wars
description: Comedians Dave Anthony and Gareth Reynolds on Glasgow’s 1980s “Ice Cream Wars”, when gangs fought over van routes used to sell drugs and stolen goods; a 1984 arson in the Ruchazie housing scheme killed six of the Doyle family.
